messages:
Jules: quick heads-up — i did a light audit of tool-calling + structured-output pages and flagged a few TS examples that still use the legacy function_call shape and an out-of-date import path in the tools registry. can we triage?

Priya: i can take the TS snippets and the registry. which files are highest priority?

Jules: added a short grep + list to the issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/1024. main hotspots: /docs/examples/ts/, /docs/guides/tool-calling/, and /docs/reference/tools-registry.md. also saw a couple of external blog links pointing at old example slugs.

Owen: i'll handle redirects for external/old slugs and move deleted examples into docs/legacy-tools/. i'll open PR A for just the redirects so CI is simpler.

Marcy: we should also add a tiny test demonstrating parser fallback order (schema -> compact envelope -> heuristics) so docs + examples have an executable reference. i can add a jest example under /docs/examples/parse-tests/parse-order.test.ts.

Priya: working on the TS snippets. propuesta for a canonical migrate snippet: 
```
// old
const resp = await client.chat.completions.create({ model: 'gpt-x', function_call: { name: 'get_profile' } });
// new
import { getProfile } from '../../examples/tools/getProfile';
const resp = await client.chat.completions.create({ model: 'gpt-x', tools: [getProfile] });
```
Will include a short comment about adding a JSON schema for the tool args and how to prefer explicit property types.

Jules: perfect. also update tools-registry.md to show the new export path and a tiny table with "name" vs "handler signature" so authors don't accidentally export the wrong shape.

Owen: opened PR A: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5123 (redirects + legacy moves). tagging @Priya @Marcy for follow-ups.

LinkBot: automated: linkcheck found 7 broken links (full list attached to CI): https://ci.redwood-inference.internal/links/5123. failing refs include /examples/old-getProfile.md and /examples/ts/old-tool-snippet.md.

Priya: started PR B branch docs/snippets/ts-tool-migrate-pri-5129. i'll push the TS snippets update, the updated registry page, and a 3-line migration note in /docs/migration.md that points to the parse-test and new canonical snippet.

Marcy: added the jest parse-order test locally. sample test shows the ordering and a small mock of the parser:
```
test('parser fallback order', () => {
  // mock response that could match schema or envelope
  const resp = '{"summary": "x"}';
  // assert schema parser wins over heuristics in our harness
});
```
I'll flesh it out and include instructions in the docs page for running the test.

Jules: split-approved. PR A for low-risk redirects only, PR B for snippets + tests + migration note. keeps rollbacks easy.

Owen: PR A merged. legacy files moved to /docs/legacy-tools/ with short readme lines.

Priya: PR B opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5129 — includes: updated TS snippets, updated tools-registry.md, parse-order test reference, and migration note. request reviews from @Jules and @Marcy.

Marcy: reviewed PR B. left a small nit: expand the migration note to call out older SDKs that may not support tools=[..] yet and suggest a compatibility shim.

Priya: addressed nit and added the shim snippet for older SDKs (one-liner wrapper). pushed changelist.

LinkBot: automated: docs preview built: https://deploy-preview.redwood-inference.io/preview/5129 — build passed.

Jules: reviewed and approved. left one tiny wording suggestion on tools-registry examples.

Priya: applied wording tweak, rebased and merged PR B. :tada:

LinkBot: automated: post-merge linkcheck run passed. no remaining broken links in affected areas.

Jules: thanks team. follow-ups: 1) @Marcy please add a short README in /docs/examples/parse-tests/ explaining how to run the test harness locally, 2) i'll open a quick issue to sweep Python snippets later (less urgent), 3) if you see external references to the old slugs ping me and i'll add permanent redirects.

Marcy: will add the README in a separate PR tomorrow.

Priya: happy to help with Python sweep when you open the issue.

Jules: closing this thread. great job — cleaner examples + testable docs now. :rocket:
